newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies close up sharply, hogs mostly up.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies close up sharply, hogs mostly up.

text.p: CME pork belly futures closed sharply higher after a near limit up rally late when firm cash and strong technicals added to demand from Tuesday's bullish out-of-town report, traders said.
Pork bellies finished 2.450 to 1.025 cent higher with February up most at 71.850 cents. That month was up 2.900 cents at one time.

Futures bulged from the start following the lighter than expected in-movement at out-of-town warehouses last week. Technical buying then kept the market supported with a firmer cash belly market adding to late strength, they said.
The CME reported an in-movement last week at approved warehouses of 1.383 million lbs, about one third of last year's in-movement of 3.7 million lbs.
Cash bellies were firmer at noon and the lighter storings shows better than expected demand for product, they said.

"Based on the (hog) slaughter levels and where the cash market is, we are looking at fairly good price/supply balance at the moment," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
Hog futures also benefited from higher belly futures prices. Sharp gains there provided spillover support which added to strength from improved cash conditions during the day, traders said.
"The cash market started out a half (dollar) lower but packers showed a little increase in demand as the morning wore on," Levitt said.

Expectations of stronger cash hog markets going into Thanksgiving also encouraged support. The futures market usually starts to rally after mid November and may have started early this year, they said.
But December ran into technical resistance. The market looks overbought on the charts, they added.
Rand Financials remained a notable buyer in nearbys with Rosenthal Collins, R.J. O'Brien and ADM Investor Services sellers during the day, pit sources said.
In hog options, volatility was firm in February and April. R.J. O'Brien spread long June 70 puts/short June 82 calls, pit sources said.
Hog futures closed 0.600 cent higher to 0.125 lower with December up most at 56.800 cents.
